environment: fresh Vultr VMs (one per run), gVisor sandbox, Burner fake internet
method: red-team repo (samples/redteam-escape) run as the 'take-home' through the normal scan path

tests.detail: Answered by Burner's fake internet with a fake {} — the real site was never reached.
Raw-IP request was captured by the fake internet; nothing left the VM.
Query was intercepted and got a fake answer (198.18.0.4); 8.8.8.8 was never reached.
Got a fake {} — no Vultr instance metadata or credentials exposed.
Connection went nowhere: no SSH banner from the host.
uname reports 4.19.0-gvisor: syscalls hit gVisor's user-space kernel, not the host's.
su failed with an authentication failure.
mount of /dev/vda2 failed; the host disk is not reachable.
Originally crashed the sandbox with --pids-limit 512. Now --pids-limit 4096 --ulimit nproc=400 caps it at 396 processes and the sandbox survives.
The sandbox dies but the host is fine; Burner reports SANDBOX_DIED and the verdict is SUSPICIOUS — never clean.
The content-safety model (nemotron) called the README "safe", i.e. missed the injection, but the planner ignored it and the rule-based verdict stayed MALICIOUS.
0 packets forwarded from the sandbox bridge to the real internet.

defender.when: at write time (the folderOpen VS Code task)
defender.note: Defender caught one sample file by signature and none of the 12 stealers; Burner judges by behaviour instead.
